channel.title: Vision For Xperiences — News
channel.description: VFX, 3D animation, live visuals, interactive installations and drone work, from the Vision For Xperiences studio desk.

item.title: Generative 3D just learned to think like a printer
item.description: Meshy AI's print-ready pipeline turns prompts into physical objects, and the tooling finally matches the speed of digital design.

item.title: Blender agents just learned to write cleaner geometry than humans
item.description: 3D-Agent shipped a standalone app in September that rewrites its own scripts for quad topology. Agentic workflows just stopped being a side project.

item.title: Vicon just bought markerless facial capture, and the integration matters
item.description: Head-mounted cameras for facial performance capture are now part of a full-body mocap pipeline. Here is what that changes.

item.title: Mesh generation just stopped being a bottleneck
item.description: Meshy 7.1 launched this September with geometry that holds up at 4K resolution. What changes when the hardest part of 3D work becomes instant.

item.title: When your editor can handle VFX and when you actually need a studio
item.description: It depends on the shot, the timeline, the software cost, and whether you can afford to go back and redo it.

item.title: Blender 5.3 ships animation chains that stop fighting back
item.description: Forward compatibility for spline IK and better pose workflows mean less time wrestling rigs and more time shipping.

item.title: Adobe and ChatGPT just automated industrial product visualization
item.description: Conversational image generation for industrial marketing moved from science fiction to October 1st, and the workflow math changed.

item.title: EEVEE Next closes the realism gap, and real-time just got serious
item.description: Blender's rebuilt ray-traced engine shipped with unlimited lights and screen-space reflections. For studios balancing speed and fidelity, the rules just changed.

item.title: MAPP_MTL turned Montreal into a projection canvas, and the tooling caught up
item.description: AI is automating the hardest part of building for curved façades. Here is what changed for large-scale mapping.

item.title: Markerless mocap just became free, and the stage disappeared
item.description: Epic and Move AI shipped better video-based motion capture this summer. The tools are fast enough that a phone camera in a room becomes the whole rig.

item.title: Maxon Redshift just plugged into Vectorworks, and the handoff vanished
item.description: Architects can now move from real-time preview to production render inside the same app. Here is what changes when the file doesn't leave the house.

item.title: Finding a drone operator who is actually licensed and insured
item.description: One license covers 30 countries. Insurance is mandatory for work. Here is how to check.

item.title: The largest LED volume just opened, and the math changed for everyone
item.description: A 50-meter curved wall in China marks the scale where virtual production stops being niche. For smaller studios, that means the rental market is about to shift.

item.title: ComfyUI added inpaint canvas, and masking just got faster
item.description: A new custom node turns ComfyUI into a layered paint program. It cuts the friction between generation and refinement.

item.title: Luxury brands now shoot nothing: the rise of pure CGI campaigns
item.description: Major fashion houses are abandoning photoshoots entirely for controlled, perfect 3D renders. Here's what that means for everyone making product visuals.

item.title: Three.js made the WebGPU swap a one-liner, and adoption jumped to 65 percent
item.description: When the most-used 3D library for web work lets you swap renderers in one line, adoption stops being theoretical. Here's what changed for people building in the browser.

item.title: Nodi just made node graphs codeable, and the loop closed
item.description: Drive a node graph from your code editor. No more hand-wiring the procedural workflow.

item.title: The free tools finally arrived, and they are boring now
item.description: The gap between open source and commercial software is not a talking point anymore. It is just the landscape.

item.title: One studio or many: hiring for VFX, animation and live visuals together
item.description: Boutique houses with multiple disciplines cost more than specialists but keep files and clients in one place. Here's what to look for and who actually does this work.

item.title: Real-world NeRF is finally about the capture, not just the math
item.description: The latest neural reconstruction work solves motion blur and sparse input. That changes what you actually shoot on set.

item.title: Meshy just plugged AI mesh generation into Claude and other coding assistants
item.description: When text-to-3D becomes a native capability of AI agents, the abstraction between describing something and building it dissolves.

item.title: Free AI rigging just removed the skeleton-building tax
item.description: Armature automates the repetitive part of character rigging and ships free, which changes the economics of projects where rigs matter but budgets don't.

item.title: WebGPU just went baseline across every browser
item.description: Native-class 3D performance in the browser is no longer a future idea. The platform just changed.

item.title: Meshy opens the text-to-physical pipeline at CES 2026
item.description: An AI model generator that shapes output to real manufacturing constraints changes who can turn a render into an actual object.

item.title: One studio or many: when to hire specialists instead
item.description: A handful of studios do handle previz through delivery, but 2026's trend is smarter handoffs with specialists.

item.title: Houdini 22 plugs AI agents into character rigging
item.description: SideFX wired MCP code generation into KineFX, letting riggers scaffold procedural setups faster without losing control.

item.title: DJI Avata 360 turns FPV from a directional choice into a spatial capture tool
item.description: 360-degree eight-kilohertz video means pilots can now shoot the whole moment and choose the angle in post.

item.title: ISO 22028-5 finally gives HDR stills a shared language
item.description: A new standard published in May defines how to encode and store HDR photographs with colour you can trust across devices.

item.title: Vicon acquires face capture firm, closing the pipeline gap
item.description: Facial and body performance capture have always come from different vendors. That just changed.

item.title: Vendor lock-in is now the top reason studios pick open tools
item.description: Clients increasingly demand ownership of their pipelines. That changes how studios pitch and what they budget for.
